::: {.brief-meta}
**Question.** Which precision, decoder, and serving profile should be the daily driver?
**Decision.** Choose the Qwen quality and throughput profile to run as the daily driver, then choose the next comparable evaluation needed to confirm or revise that choice.
**Reader.** self.
:::

## Summary

Use official [FP8](#fp8-and-nvfp4) on vLLM `v0.28.0` with [DFlash2](#dflash2) K7, an FP8 [KV cache](#kv-cache), [automatic prefix caching](#automatic-prefix-caching), Qwen [tool parsers](#tool-parser), and low reasoning as the daily driver; keep the RadixArk [NVFP4](#fp8-and-nvfp4) BF16-head lane as the checkpoint-only challenger [@local-serving-config; @local-litellm-routing; @qwen-fp8-card].

- The repository configures six Qwen lanes, but configuration, historical observation, proposal, and current verification are separate evidence states [@local-serving-config; @local-historical-observations].
- First-party provenance favors official FP8 for quality, while a matched community DGX Spark comparison supports NVFP4 only as a throughput hypothesis for this host [@qwen-fp8-card; @radixark-bf16-lmhead-card; @dgx-fp8-nvfp4].
- Decoder counts, hybrid-cache behavior, open [SM120](#sm120) defects, and dated local runs limit how far any result transfers [@dflash2-card; @vllm-issue-53726; @vllm-issue-54360; @vllm-issue-54623].
- Quality, capacity, tool reliability, portability, and lifecycle risk favor FP8 for daily work until the faster mixed-precision lane passes the whole request path [@vllm-tool-calling; @local-audit-evidence; @rtx6kpro-common-issues].
- A checkpoint-only FP8-versus-RadixArk comparison with fixed serving controls would most directly confirm or overturn the choice [@local-serving-config; @local-audit-evidence].

## Glossary

### Automatic prefix caching {#automatic-prefix-caching}

vLLM automatic prefix caching reuses hash-identified KV blocks from an earlier request with the same token prefix and cache identity [@vllm-prefix-cache].

### DFlash2 {#dflash2}

DFlash2 is a separate block-diffusion draft checkpoint whose candidates the target model verifies before returning tokens [@dflash2-card].

### FP8 and NVFP4 {#fp8-and-nvfp4}

FP8 and NVIDIA FP4 are floating-point formats used by the named checkpoints in different mixed-precision layouts; the format label alone does not identify which layers stay at higher precision [@qwen-fp8-card; @radixark-bf16-lmhead-card; @unsloth-nvfp4-card].

### Gated DeltaNet {#gated-deltanet}

Gated DeltaNet is the recurrent linear-attention component in Qwen3.8-27B's hybrid architecture [@qwen-bf16-card].

### KV cache {#kv-cache}

The key-value cache stores attention state from processed tokens so later generation does not recompute that state [@vllm-prefix-cache].

### Multi-token prediction {#mtp}

Multi-token prediction uses a prediction head embedded in the target checkpoint to propose future tokens for verification [@sglang-qwen-cookbook; @ninfer-card].

### SM120 {#sm120}

SM120 is the NVIDIA Blackwell compute target named in the cited vLLM reports for the RTX 5090-class failure paths [@vllm-issue-52540; @vllm-issue-53726].

### Tool parser {#tool-parser}

A tool parser converts model output into the structured `tool_calls` contract expected by an OpenAI-compatible client [@vllm-tool-calling].

## Local profiles have four evidence states

The checked-in files prove configuration and routing, not which backend is active or which digest a prior process resolved [@local-serving-config; @local-litellm-routing].

| Profile | Evidence state |
|---|---|
| Official FP8 on vLLM | **Configured; proposed daily driver.** FP8 KV, DFlash2 K7, prefix caching, and Qwen parsers are present [@local-serving-config]. |
| Unsloth Dynamic NVFP4 on vLLM | **Configured; historically observed.** Dated reports of loops, early stops, and failed tool calls apply to that checkpoint and older stacks [@unsloth-nvfp4-card; @local-historical-observations]. |
| RadixArk NVFP4 with BF16 head on vLLM | **Configured; historically measured.** FP8 E4M3 KV, 16,384 batched tokens, DFlash2 K7, and the SM120 kernel exclusion are present [@local-serving-config]. |
| RadixArk NVFP4 with BF16 head on SGLang | **Configured; historically measured.** DFlash2 K8, LPM scheduling, radix caching, and bounded recurrent-state storage are present [@local-serving-config; @sglang-qwen-cookbook]. |
| QUASAR NVFP4 on vLLM | **Configured; unverified here** [@local-serving-config; @local-litellm-routing]. |
| Qwen NInfer | **Configured; unverified here.** It uses an engine-specific artifact [@local-serving-config; @ninfer-card]. |

A dated vLLM control recorded 277.253 output tokens per second; a separate SGLang K8 canary recorded 266.966 [@local-historical-observations]. Different engines and configurations make these historical operating points, not a head-to-head result.

## FP8 leads the precision evidence

No fetched source supplies a same-revision, same-harness BF16, official FP8, and NVFP4 quality matrix. The evidence instead defines a quality control and a throughput challenger [@qwen-bf16-card; @qwen-fp8-card; @radixark-bf16-lmhead-card].

| Weight profile | What the evidence supports | Daily-driver use |
|---|---|---|
| BF16 | First-party capability reference with no local acceptance run in the evidence snapshot [@qwen-bf16-card; @local-historical-observations]. | Reference when a fit-safe control is practical. |
| Official FP8 | Qwen documents fine-grained FP8 with block size 128 and describes its metrics as nearly identical to BF16, but publishes no controlled precision delta [@qwen-fp8-card]. | Best available quality provenance; use now. |
| RadixArk NVFP4 with BF16 head | The third-party recipe preserves BF16 embeddings and output head and publishes its own text evaluations [@radixark-bf16-lmhead-card]. | Faster candidate that needs local acceptance. |
| Unsloth NVFP4 | The third-party dynamic recipe has its own template and serving guidance; dated checkpoint-specific reports describe behavioral failures on older stacks [@unsloth-nvfp4-card; @local-historical-observations]. | Lower-priority experiment. |

A community DGX Spark comparison held vLLM `0.27.1`, hardware, concurrency, and random workloads constant. At 16 concurrent requests, Unsloth NVFP4 produced 29% to 34% more output tokens per second than official FP8 [@dgx-fp8-nvfp4]. It supports a throughput test, not local quality or performance claims for the RTX PRO 5000, vLLM `v0.28.0`, DFlash2, or RadixArk.

FP8 stays primary; RadixArk gets one challenge.

## Decoder, cache, and hardware evidence has sharp boundaries

Decoder, cache, and kernel choices interact with Qwen3.8's hybrid full-attention and [Gated DeltaNet](#gated-deltanet) state. Results transfer only when the checkpoint, engine, speculation, cache geometry, and GPU path match.

### DFlash2 and MTP count different units

| Decoder path | Published or configured unit | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM DFlash2 | Seven speculative candidates for the checkpoint's eight-token block [@dflash2-card; @vllm-qwen-recipe]. | Matches the configured vLLM K7 lane [@local-serving-config]. |
| SGLang DFlash2 | An eight-token draft block [@dflash2-card; @sglang-qwen-cookbook]. | The different spelling does not justify changing vLLM to K8. |
| Native [MTP](#mtp) | An embedded prediction head, with no separate draft checkpoint [@sglang-qwen-cookbook; @ninfer-card]. | Lower checkpoint overhead, but open vLLM hybrid-state failures block its use on this pinned runtime [@vllm-issue-53726]. |
| NInfer MTP | An engine-specific artifact with prompt-dependent acceptance [@ninfer-card]. | Evidence that proposals can work, not evidence that NInfer beats DFlash2. |

On one RTX 5090 at concurrency one, the SGLang cookbook reports 4.92 ms median time per output token for DFlash2 and native-MTP rates of 152.9 and 144.5 output tokens per second under two recurrent-state precisions [@sglang-qwen-cookbook]. These are setup-specific operating points.

### Prefix reuse has a lifecycle

vLLM hashes complete token blocks with the parent hash and request identity, protects referenced matches during use, releases them when requests finish, and evicts unreferenced blocks under pressure [@vllm-prefix-cache]. DFlash2 begins after prefill, so it cannot account for time saved by a repeated prompt prefix [@dflash2-card].

```text
request tokens
  -> full-block hash chain
  -> matching KV blocks acquire references
  -> prefill computes the unmatched suffix
  -> DFlash2 proposes during decode
  -> request releases references
  -> memory pressure may evict free blocks
```

The diagram separates prefix prefill from speculative decode.

The stack persists model and vLLM caches beneath `/mnt/models` [@local-serving-config]. Version or selectively invalidate JIT caches after runtime or kernel changes because stale Blackwell artifacts have caused failures [@rtx6kpro-common-issues]. Local sleep/wake remains disabled in favor of container unload [@local-serving-config]. Wake readiness is unknown because the earlier consolidation note did not preserve verifiable upstream fix references.

### Three SM120 hazards have different scope

| Hazard | Current evidence | Decision boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Unsloth FP8 KV calibration | Open issue #54623 reports that Qwen3.5-family loading drops the exact Unsloth checkpoint's calibrated K/V scales; the open fix is PR #54624 [@vllm-issue-54623; @vllm-pr-54624]. Local config records the limitation [@local-serving-config]. | Treat BF16 KV as the Unsloth quality canary. The report does not establish the same failure for the official FP8 target. |
| Mixed-precision FP8 linear kernel | Open issue #52540 reports an SM120 failure in the FlashInfer FP8 scaled-matrix-multiplication lane [@vllm-issue-52540]. | Keep the kernel exclusion on affected local mixed-NVFP4 lanes; do not copy it to unrelated profiles without confirming dispatch [@local-serving-config]. |
| Hybrid speculation and cache | Open issues report illegal memory access under native MTP and reduced or missing prefix hits when hybrid models combine caching with MTP or DFlash [@vllm-issue-53726; @vllm-issue-54360]. | Keep native MTP out of vLLM `v0.28.0`; measure DFlash cache hits instead of assuming them. |

Issue #54623 reports GSM8K accuracy of 92.3% with unit-scale FP8 KV, 93.7% with calibration, and 94.5% for its BF16-KV control [@vllm-issue-54623]. This is a checkpoint-specific reporter result, not local accuracy.

## The daily-driver tradeoff spans the complete request path

The daily driver must preserve quality, useful context, valid tools, sustained-load stability, and reproducibility. A public token rate cannot settle all five.

| Dimension | Current choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Quality | Official FP8 | First-party provenance and no controlled local evidence that a four-bit candidate preserves the failure-sensitive workload [@qwen-fp8-card; @local-audit-evidence]. |
| Throughput | RadixArk remains the challenger | Community measurements support an NVFP4 throughput hypothesis, while its BF16 head and checkpoint differ from the measured Unsloth pair [@dgx-fp8-nvfp4; @radixark-bf16-lmhead-card]. |
| Context capacity | Read startup-reported context and KV capacity | `auto` model length and FP8 KV do not guarantee a particular admitted concurrency before startup profiling [@local-serving-config; @rtx6kpro-common-issues]. |
| Decoder portability | DFlash2 on the two configured engines | vLLM and SGLang use different counters; NInfer remains engine-specific [@dflash2-card; @sglang-qwen-cookbook; @ninfer-card]. |
| Operations | Pin image identity, preserve model caches, invalidate changed JIT artifacts, and keep sleep/wake disabled | Mutable images and stale compiled state prevent comparable runs; wake safety is not established for this profile [@local-serving-config; @rtx6kpro-common-issues]. |

A skill call crosses four contracts:

```text
OpenCode skill name and description
  -> LiteLLM request and reasoning transform
  -> llama-swap route and model chat template
  -> vLLM model output and tool parser
  -> structured tool_calls returned to OpenCode
```

OpenCode loads `SKILL.md` after the model invokes the skill tool [@opencode-skills]. LiteLLM maps reasoning controls into Qwen chat-template arguments [@local-callback-policy]. vLLM automatic tool selection requires automatic choice and a parser, and the local lanes supply both [@vllm-tool-calling; @local-serving-config].

A community DGX Spark test reported one prompt-injection failure under its thinking sampler and a pass under greedy decoding [@dgx-decoder-tool]. That scenario belongs in the local evaluation, not a universal sampler ranking. The FP8 route advertises only low reasoning, but this briefing sent no request through it [@local-litellm-routing; @local-callback-policy].

The earlier audit rejected unpublished 93% to 97% MCP rankings and retained four non-Qwen comparison arms [@local-audit-evidence]:

| Comparison arm | Role in a future evaluation |
|---|---|
| Muse Glimmer | Tool-use and recovery comparison. |
| GLM-4.7-Flash | Lightweight tool-worker comparison. |
| Gemma 4 31B | Dense model and parser interoperability comparison. |
| gpt-oss-120b | High-memory tool-use control. |

These remain unproven replacements. Their evidence sits in the [Muse](../muse-context/index.qmd), [Gemma](../gemma-serving/index.qmd), and [model-memory](../model-memory/index.qmd) briefings.

## A controlled endpoint comparison can close the gap

Compare official FP8 with RadixArk NVFP4 plus the BF16 head. Change only the checkpoint first; simultaneous KV, decoder, sampler, or scheduler changes would prevent attribution.

| Control | Fixed or changed | Evidence to record |
|---|---|---|
| Target checkpoint | **Changed:** official FP8 versus RadixArk NVFP4 BF16-head. | Exact model revision and loaded weight format. |
| Serving path | **Fixed:** vLLM `v0.28.0`, DFlash2 K7, FP8 KV, kernel selection, prefix cache, Qwen parsers, template behavior, limits, and low reasoning [@local-serving-config; @local-callback-policy]. | Effective image digest, startup-resolved context, KV capacity, and scheduler budgets. |
| Workload | **Fixed:** request order, warmup, sampling, and 20 to 40 real agent prompts covering skill selection, tool rejection, nested arguments, recovery, long-context retrieval, coding, and prompt injection [@local-audit-evidence]. | Raw envelopes before and after LiteLLM, generated tokens, and finish reasons. |
| Success measures | **Fixed:** valid tool structure, completed task, loops, instruction violations, token use, latency, DFlash acceptance, cache hits, queue depth, preemptions, and process errors. | Per-arm results and run-to-run spread. |
| Promotion rule | RadixArk replaces FP8 only if it meets the FP8 behavioral gates and improves the production-shaped latency or capacity target. | A faster arm fails if parser, retrieval, instruction following, or sustained-load stability regresses. |

Resolve the mutable fastokens image tag to a digest before the comparison [@local-serving-config]. If neither arm returns stable structured calls, diagnose the request path before drawing a precision conclusion.

## Worked example

### A repeated long agent prefix

The quality-first lane expands to this vLLM argument vector; its fastokens image tag remains mutable [@local-serving-config]:

```text
Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
--served-model-name qwen3.8-27b-fp8
--enable-prefix-caching
--max-num-seqs 128
--max-model-len auto
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
--speculative-config {"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}
--reasoning-parser qwen3
--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--performance-mode throughput
```

This profile combines repeated-prefix reuse, speculative decode, and structured tool parsing. Its digest, resolved context, and KV capacity require startup observation.

A long agent session sends the same system instructions, skill catalogue, tool schemas, and early conversation twice, changing only the final user request.

1. On the cold request, vLLM tokenizes the prefix, computes complete cache blocks, and retains reusable blocks after completion [@vllm-prefix-cache].
2. On the warm request, identical token IDs and cache identity fields recover those blocks. A dated local probe on an earlier configured lane used a 58.8K-token shared prefix and recorded time to first token falling from 12.414 seconds cold to 1.018 and 1.010 seconds warm [@local-historical-observations]. This briefing did not reproduce that result on the FP8 lane.
3. DFlash2 begins helping during generation. Its acceptance and decode rate do not explain the saved prefill time [@dflash2-card].
4. Changing system text, template output, tool-schema order, model state, or another identity field can break the hash chain before the final request. The warm request then reuses fewer blocks [@vllm-prefix-cache].
5. An open hybrid-model report says speculation can reduce hits for matching prompts [@vllm-issue-54360]. Keep the checkpoint and request fixed, then run DFlash2 on and off. Record output, cache-hit deltas, time to first token, and acceptance. Pass only if output remains correct and cache loss does not erase the end-to-end benefit.

The historical probe shows the prefix benefit. The DFlash control tests whether it survives speculation; the outcome is unverified.

## Limitations

No backend was started and no benchmark was run. Local rates and cache timings are dated observations in `sources/evidence.json`; model cards provide vendor evidence, and NVIDIA forum posts provide community measurements. No fetched source supplies a controlled local matrix across the three precision families, two engines, and two decoders.

The active backend, image digest, resolved context, KV capacity, prefix hits, and sustained-load stability remain unverified. Issue #54623 and PR #54624 were open when fetched on 2026-09-09 [@vllm-issue-54623; @vllm-pr-54624]. Sleep/wake stays disabled until a future wake regression because the evidence set does not establish fix readiness.

## Next action

Pin the custom fastokens image by digest, then run the checkpoint-only FP8-versus-RadixArk comparison through the complete agent request path. Keep FP8 as the daily driver until RadixArk passes the behavioral and sustained-load gates.
